٭٭٭

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 12, verse 102:

Lesson 111: Explanation of the verses 102 to 111

Here the actual story of Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) ends, and now instructive comments are made on it. While commenting on this surah, we pointed out the aims and purposes for which this story was related in detail. Here, now, the readers are turned to several matters for admonition, and their feelings are awakened. Human thought is set running through the vastness of this universe and the depths of the human self. The circumstances of past peoples, present conditions, and the hidden realities behind the veil of the unseen are described. Accordingly, we take the realities stated in this final comment in the same order, because this Qur'anic order is also based on wisdom.

٭٭٭

This story was not well known among the Arabs; the Arab society in which the Messenger ﷺ was raised was unaware of these events. Among these very people the Prophet ﷺ was sent. Since the characters of this story had, in their circumstances, better secrets and mysteries, even though they were characters of centuries past, Allah, the Exalted, called it the best of stories at the very beginning of the surah.

﴿We relate to you the best of stories, in that We have revealed to you this Qur'an, although before it you were certainly among the unaware﴾ (12:3). And now, at the conclusion of this story, the sequel comes in such a way that the ending also points back to its beginning.

Verse No. 102

This story, which has been related in the preceding pages, is among the news of the unseen which no one knew except Allah. You did not know it either, and We revealed it to you. And this is a living miracle, O Messenger. You were not present with them when they were devising their plot, especially when they had prepared their plan of action, the details of which have been given throughout this whole story. They plotted against Yusuf (peace be upon him), and they also plotted against their father. Then, when Yusuf (peace be upon him) seized his brother, these people withdrew and began consulting together, and this was a plot, that is, a scheme, on their part. Moreover, in it there were also the cunning schemes of the women against Yusuf (peace be upon him). Then in it there was also the cunning of the parliament of the Chief of Egypt, in that they sent Prophet Yusuf (peace be upon him) to prison unjustly. All of this was a plot, and O Messenger, you had no knowledge of any of these stratagems. You were not present at the time that you could have recorded it with such detail. Rather, it is revelation, and through it is intended to establish the fundamental beliefs of this new outlook on life and new religion. And this story has various scenes and views. The issues and ideas of this new outlook on life are scattered throughout it.

٭٭٭

This story proves that this speech is the revelation of Allah. Its allusions, impressions and guidance stir hearts, and all of these demand that people then believe in this speech. Especially since these people are also aware of the personal circumstances of the Messenger ﷺ. They know him well, and he gives them, before their eyes, such admonitory, unseen and engaging news, yet despite this, the majority of people do not accept it sincerely. The majority of people see the signs and miracles scattered throughout this universe day and night, but no awareness comes to them. These people do not grasp the meaning of these signs and proofs, like a blind person who turns from one side to the other and is not aware of anything. The question is: after this miraculous story, what are these people waiting for now? Are they waiting for a punishment of Allah that will seize them suddenly while they have no awareness?

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 12, verses 103–107:

Verses 103 to 107

The Messenger of Allah ﷺ desired most intensely that his people would believe. He wished that the good he had brought would reach them, and that they would not be deprived of it. Moreover, he felt compassion for his people: if they remained in polytheism, they would see evil days in this world, and in the Hereafter they would remain in everlasting punishment. But Allah is very near to the hearts of human beings; He is All-Knowing and All-Aware. He is thoroughly acquainted with human temperament and their circumstances. Therefore, the Prophet ﷺ is told that this eagerness and this intense desire of his will not be able to turn them toward Islam, and most of them will remain polytheists, because these people pass by the signs of Allah without heed; they turn away from them, and this very aversion is the obstacle in their path, preventing them from believing. They do not benefit from the proofs scattered throughout this universe.

You are only charged with conveying the message. If these people do not believe, you suffer no loss. You do not ask any reward from them for this task. Yet, despite this, these people turn away and avert their faces from guidance, although this guidance is being provided to them free of charge.

﴿Verily, it is nothing but a reminder for all the worlds﴾ (12:104). You are reminding them of the signs of Allah, and you wish to turn both their sight and their insight toward the path of guidance. This guidance is for all the worlds; it is not confined to one people, a particular lineage, or a specific tribe. Its price is not fixed such that some are unable to pay it, so that only the wealthy could purchase it while the poor could not. Nor is there a condition of physical strength for its attainment, so that the strong could acquire it while the weak are incapable of doing so. It is an open reminder for all the worlds. It is an open table to which all people are invited; whoever wishes may accept it.

﴿And how many a sign in the heavens and the earth do they pass by, while they turn away from it﴾ (12:105). The signs that testify to the Divine Being, that point to Allah's oneness and power, are scattered everywhere in this universe, inviting the sight and insight of people to contemplation. They are in the heavens and on the earth, and people observe them morning and evening. At night they are before them, and in the morning as well. They call out to people, calling loudly, and they are so manifest that nothing stands between people's eyes and them. They invite the human heart and vision to reflection, yet people neither see them, nor pay heed to their call, nor does their awareness awaken when they are shaken.

Just pause for a moment and reflect on the rising and setting of the sun; pause and reflect on how the shadows of trees lengthen and shorten in an imperceptible manner. Look at the boundless sea; look at the springs gushing forth from the earth; observe the flowing rivers; look at the birds flying in the sky; then look at the colourful fish swimming beneath the water; look at the creeping insects on the surface of the earth; observe the great host of ants and other insects and creatures, and the living beings that cannot even be seen; and observe the alternation of night and day, the tranquillity of the night and the joys of the day. A single moment of reflection can open for a person the doors to the wonders of this universe. This brief and thoughtful moment alone can create a wide vibration in the world of human perception, and a person can respond to the call of the natural universe. But﴿they pass by them, yet they remain heedless of them﴾ (12:105). And this is why most of these people do not believe. Then, even among those who have believed, polytheism has entered their thoughts and vision in some way. Therefore, pure faith requires that it remain alert and vigilant at all times and in every moment, and that it expel from the heart every kind of satanic whisper. It must purify the heart from every kind of worldly defilement. In every thought, every action, and every kind of disposition and undertaking, it must keep the pleasure of Allah in view. Every deed and every initiative should be for Allah. Pure faith is that which pervades a person's heart and mind, which fully governs a person's speech, actions and conduct, and which influences a person in such a way that no other than Allah retains sovereignty over his life. A person should not worship anyone other than Allah in any of his affairs, and he should be the servant of that Ruler whose command no one can reject.

﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they associate others with Him﴾ (12:106). How are these people polytheists? They commit shirk in determining the value of events, things and persons on this earth. In seeking benefit and in protecting people from harm, they look for means other than the power and decree of Allah alone. They regard certain personalities and institutions, other than Allah and His law, as the source of guidance and the means of law and sharia. They place their hopes in others than Allah, and they make sacrifices and charities in which, beneath the surface, the pleasure of some personalities other than the pleasure of Allah is present and considered. They strive in vain to obtain benefit from others than Allah or to avert harm, or in the worship of Allah they take into account the pleasure of others besides the pleasure of Allah. This is hidden shirk (shirk khafi), and for this reason the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Shirk enters among you so imperceptibly that it is like the sound of an ant's movement."

The Prophet ﷺ mentioned several examples through which hidden shirk may be understood. Imam al-Tirmidhi narrated from Ibn Umar: "Whoever swears by other than Allah has committed shirk." Imam Abu Dawud, Imam Ahmad and others narrated from Ibn Mas'ud (may Allah be pleased with him): "The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: incantations (ruqyah), amulets and charms are shirk." In the Musnad of Imam Ahmad, a hadith of Uqbah ibn Amir is narrated: The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Whoever hangs an amulet has committed shirk."

Abu Hurairah (may Allah be pleased with him) narrated with the same chain that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "Allah says: I am not in need of partners' partnership. Whoever performs an action in which he associates another with Me, I leave him to that other."

Imam Ahmad narrated from Abu Sa'id ibn Fadalah, who said: I heard the Messenger of Allah ﷺ say: "When Allah gathers the first and the last on that day about which there is no doubt, a caller will call out: whoever associated with Allah a partner in an act that was exclusively for Allah, let him seek his reward from that partner, for Allah has no need of partners' partnership."

Imam Ahmad narrated through his chain from Mahmud ibn Labid that the Messenger of Allah ﷺ said: "I warn you of the lesser shirk, which causes me concern." The Companions said: "O Messenger of Allah, what is the lesser shirk?" He said: "It is ostentation (riya'). On the Day of Resurrection, when people come with their deeds, Allah will say: Go to those for whose sake you used to show off in the world, and see whether you find any reward with them."

In sum, despite faith, these are the kinds of hidden shirk. A believer should remain vigilant about them and strive to avoid them, so that his faith may become pure.

Apart from hidden shirk, there are certain clear acts of shirk, and among them is the conduct of a person who follows the religion and system of someone other than Allah in any matter of life. For example, he gets decisions made, or makes them, according to a law that opposes the sharia. This act is a manifest, explicit and clear shirk about which there is no difference of opinion. Likewise, establishing urs and fairs that Allah has not prescribed, or other customs and traditions for which there is no proof from the sharia, or clothing in which the covering of 'awrah and other injunctions of the sharia are violated. All of these are plainly acts of shirk.

Those matters connected with customs and ceremonies that are contrary to Islam, which have been introduced by someone other than Allah, and which people consider necessary to follow in the same manner as the commands of Allah and His Messenger, such practices and customs do not remain mere sins; they attain the status of shirk, because by following them a person follows a religion and system other than Allah's, one that is opposed to the Islamic system. In this respect, the matter is extremely important, dangerous, and amounts to shirk.

This is why Allah says:

﴿And most of them do not believe in Allah except that they associate others with Him﴾ (12:106). Therefore, this verse applies both to those who, in the Arabian Peninsula, continued to commit shirk even after believing, and to those who come after him and who believe but still commit shirk in some way.

Now the question is: what is it that these people who turn away from guidance place their hopes in? Having turned away from the Qur'anic verses, they are also turning away from the signs of the universe. What is their support after all? Do they not fear Allah?

﴿Do they feel secure that there will not come upon them an overwhelming punishment from Allah, or that the Hour will not come upon them suddenly while they do not perceive?﴾ (12:107). This is a powerful blow to the strings of their consciousness, so that they may awaken from the slumber of heedlessness and fear the evil end of that heedlessness, for the time of the punishment of Allah is known to no one; it may descend at any moment. It may seize them at any time, and this punishment may be general, or it may come in the form of that terrifying day which will appear suddenly, and no one will even be aware of it. The doors of the unseen world are closed; what lies behind the veil of the unseen no ear has heard of, and no eye can see. No one knows what will happen in the next moment, so how can a person of sound mind remain heedless?

Since the Qur'an is filled with proofs of the Messenger of Allah's prophethood, since every particle of this universe bears witness that it has one sole Creator and Sustainer, and since these people see this universe and understand the Qur'an, being Arabs themselves, and yet they commit hidden or manifest shirk with Allah, and since the majority of people are afflicted by this disease and heedlessness, what path remains for the Messenger of Allah ﷺ except to continue on his way, and for his followers to press forward toward their goal, unaffected by the deeds or words of anyone, and not looking toward those who deviate?

They are entirely apart from those who do not fully accept their ideas, who do not follow their methodology and way of working, or who do not accept their leadership. Those who do not follow their creed and manner should separate themselves from the jahili (ignorant, pre-Islamic) society, completely separate. The duty of the callers to truth is not merely to fulfil the right of conveying the call of religion and then mingle among the jahili society spread around them. A call of that kind will have no benefit. They must announce clearly that they are a distinct people, distinguished from jahiliyyah. On the basis of one ideology they must lay the foundation of a separate association and organization, and must be organized under the name and title of an Islamic leadership, and must be completely separated from this jahili society. Their leadership too must be distinguished from a jahili leadership.

To mingle into a jahili society and to live under a jahili leadership cools the strength and fervour of the Islamic worldview, and all the effects of their call are nullified. And the attractiveness that the call of Islam has when the Islamic system is established no longer remains within it.

This reality was not only a reality at the time when the Messenger ﷺ was working in the jahili society of the polytheists of Makkah; whenever jahiliyyah predominates and some Islamic movement begins its struggle against it, it must act in the same way against it. At this time, the jahiliyyah that has overspread the twentieth century is like all those jahiliyyahs against which the Islamic movements of the prophets worked in human history; all share the same features.

Those people who have the vain notion that, by remaining within the present jahili society, and by adopting the customs and ways of the present jahili society, and by remaining within those jahili societies, they will call to Islam in a very gentle manner of preaching and will reach some result, are plainly deluded. They have not understood the Islamic worldview and Islamic beliefs at all, and they do not know how the Islamic worldview enters hearts. All holders of jahili ideologies declare their goal, their method of work, and their name and title very clearly, and openly work for their aims. Is it only the callers to Islam who are left to work in secret and concealment? Yet their work has a fixed method, which is distinct from the method of jahiliyyah.

* * *

Now a point needs attention: what is Allah's sunnah regarding the messengers and their missions? And what lesson for those who come later is found in the outcome of some earlier peoples? Muhammad ﷺ is not the first prophet. Before him messengers came and presented their mission. The outcome of those who previously denied them unjustly is instructive for you.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 12, verse 109:

Verse 109

In the history of earlier peoples there is a lesson for those who come later. Therefore those who come after should study the history of those who came before. By this, hearts are softened, to the point that fear enters the hearts of even great dictators. When the activities and movements of earlier peoples are brought to life in the imagination, one sees that these people, with all their pomp and splendour, and then the scene passes before the screen of thought: look, these people have been annihilated and destroyed, they lie without sense or motion and have mingled with the dust. Their cities and habitations have taken the form of ruins, and along with them their knowledge and culture, their movement and activity, their ascendancy and their ideas have also perished. Through such imaginings and reflection, the hearts of human beings tremble, and even the most heedless person's hair stands on end from fear. This is why the Holy Qur'an recounts to people the stories of the rise and fall of earlier nations, and takes them to walk among the ruins which narrate the tales of those peoples.

﴿Wa ma arsalna ... al-qura﴾ (12:109) "And We did not send before you any but men to whom We revealed, from among the people of the towns." That is, they were neither angels nor some other strange creation, but, O Prophet, they were men like you. They were townsmen, not villagers, so that they would be refined and would listen to speech gently. Therefore, strive to bear the difficulties that arise on the path of the Islamic call, and keep guiding people to the right path. Your movement and call are also founded on the same divine way according to which God sent all the prophets. These people were human beings, and God's message was revealed to them?

﴿Afalam yasiru ... min qablihim﴾ (12:109) "Have they not travelled in the land and seen what was the end of those before them?" So that they may know that their own end will be the same as that of those who came before them, unless the divine way is about to seize them in its grip, and so that they may understand that they must surely leave this world.

﴿Wa la dar al-akhirah khayrun lilladhina ittaqaw﴾ (12:109) "Certainly the abode of the Hereafter is better for those who are God-fearing." Because there is no permanence in this world; from here one must surely depart.

﴿Afala ta'qilun﴾ (12:109) "Will you not then understand?" Do you not understand the working of the divine way in human history? And can your reason not make a sound judgment even in such a matter, that one thing is perishable and another endures, and that the perishable should be given preference over the enduring?

Now mention is made of some difficult moments in the lives of the Messengers. These difficult moments come before the final victory. These hardships are part of the divine way, and they confront the caller, because the divine way is not one that can be averted.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on Surah 12, verse 110:

Verse No. 110

This is an extremely frightening situation. Here a picture is drawn of the most painful, straitened and severely difficult circumstances in the lives of the Messengers. Such were the circumstances in which the Messengers confronted disbelief, denial, obstinacy and manifest blindness. Days passed in this way, yet the Messengers never abandoned the call, and the people continued to deny. The cycle of day and night continued in the same manner, and falsehood kept roaring. The people of falsehood were very numerous, while the believers were few and weak.

How harsh the conditions are! Falsehood is panting, committing rebellion and transgression, and oppression and aggression are its practice. In these circumstances the Messengers wait for the promise of Allah. But Allah's promise does not appear. In these circumstances, all kinds of doubts arise in their hearts. You see that they were rejected; you see that apparently their view, that they would achieve success in this world, was rejected. But this success was not attained.

When any Messenger falls into such circumstances, then constriction, severity, anguish and torment become unbearable for him. This verse, and along with it, when I read the following verse of Surah al-Baqarah:

Am hasibtum an ... nasrullah (2:214) "Do you think that you will enter Paradise while such circumstances have not come upon you as came upon those who passed before you? Misfortune and hardship touched them, and they were shaken until the Messenger and those who believed with him cried out: When will the help of Allah come?"

Whenever I read either of these two verses, I tremble with fear, that the Messengers had to confront such life-consuming difficulties. In such difficult circumstances a person is afflicted with all kinds of doubts; he continuously faces painful and shaking circumstances, in which even Messengers were shaken; a person is struck by a painful psychological struggle, and an unbearable torment constantly pursues him.

In circumstances in which this grief and sorrow is constantly visible, and the heart rises to the throat, and the Messenger and his community expend their full strength, then in such circumstances the help of Allah comes. And the help that comes in such circumstances is decisive. Jaa-hum nasruna fa-nujjiya man nashaa'u wa la yuraddu ba'suna 'anil-qawmil-mujrimin (12:110): "Suddenly Our help reached the Messengers. Then, when such a moment arrives, it is Our way that whomever We wish, We save; and from the criminal people Our punishment cannot be averted." This is the sunnah of Allah regarding the Islamic call. Difficulties must come on this path. It is necessary to face painful circumstances, until the Islamic movement expends its full strength on this path, its entire power and might is spent, extremely hopeless circumstances become apparent, and apparent means on which people rely disappear one after another. In such circumstances, then, only help from Allah comes, and only those are saved concerning whom Allah has a decree; and destruction then comes upon the opponents of the Islamic movement; those who deserve salvation are saved from it, and the destruction that comes upon the deniers does not reach them. Thus such people are freed from the oppressive and tyrannical environment that tyrants and oppressors have imposed upon them. Now hopelessness and helplessness fall to the lot of the criminals. They are ruined and destroyed, and their power is shattered. Now they have neither a protector nor a helper.

Why has this sunnah been established? So that victory and help do not become valueless, and do not become a mere jest. If victory and help were obtained without sacrifices, then everyone would rise up and become a caller, and anyone would attain success without giving any sacrifice, or would bring about a revolution by minor effort. Therefore Allah has not kept the Islamic call as easy as a mere game or amusement. The aim of the Islamic call is to bring about a revolution in the methods of entire life. And this revolution cannot be brought about by those who merely make claims, without any sacrifice behind them. Such people cannot bear the sacrifices given in the path of the Islamic call. Such people, at first, do not put their hands into a difficult task like the Islamic call; but if they do make this mistake, they cannot fulfil its due, and soon, growing helpless, they abandon it. When difficulties come in the path of truth, only the sincere and resolute people confront them, who do not abandon the path of the Islamic call under any condition, even if they become certain that they will not achieve success in this world.

The Islamic call is not a bargain that is for a limited time; nor is the profit of this bargain confined to the limited life of this world; and it is also not possible that the people who make this bargain would cancel it and become ready for some other profitable bargain through which they would quickly gain profit in this world. Those who raise the banner of the Islamic call in any jahili society (and remember that a jahili society is every society in which the commands of Allah are not obeyed, and other than Allah, the taghut are obeyed), such people should understand well that being a worker of the movement is not a matter of entertainment, nor is this work a commercial transaction for worldly benefit. It is a matter of continuous struggle against those taghut forces that possess manpower and financial power, and those taghut forces have so suppressed the masses that they call white black and black white. And the common people are helpless. Furthermore, these forces are so influential that they release the common herd like dogs upon the Islamic movements, and the method of their operation among the people is that: O people! These people will deprive you of every kind of entertainment and luxury, and will end the colourfulness of life... In short, it is the duty of the bearers of the Islamic call to understand that on this path there are nothing but thorns, and then the process of overcoming these difficulties is even more difficult. Therefore the rule is that, in the beginning, the workers of the Islamic movement are only resolute people. Common people run away from this movement. Only the chosen, preferred and resolute people of society come towards it. These people are ready to sacrifice everything for the establishment of the religion; they are ready to sacrifice all the comforts and provisions of the world. Obviously, in the beginning such people are few, but Allah decides between such people and their nation with regard to truth, and this truth becomes manifest only when long struggle is undertaken for it; and when truth comes, the matter is decided, victory is achieved, and then the general masses enter into it.

In the story of Yusuf (peace be upon him) there are manifold difficulties which this caller confronts. He is thrown into a dark well. In the house of the ruler of Egypt he lives like a servant and slave. Then he is unjustly sent to prison, and despairs of the help of people; but the final outcome is in favour of those who believe and adopt the path of taqwa, as Allah has said, and the promise of Allah is always true. The story of Yusuf is an important example among the stories of the prophets, and there is a lesson in it for every person who has intellect. In it there is also this lesson: that Hazrat Muhammad (ﷺ) had no knowledge of the circumstances of earlier prophets, yet these details were given in this story; therefore this is evidence of the truth of the Quran, for otherwise it is not possible for anyone to fabricate such circumstances from himself and have them be correct word for word; and the heart of a believer is never satisfied with artificial stories.

Commentary of Sayyid Qutb (Fi Zilal al-Quran, Urdu translation) on surah 12, verse 111:

Verse No. 111

Consider carefully how harmonious the beginning and the end of the surah are. In the same way, the beginning and the end of the story are also mutually ...... The beginning of the story also contains conclusions drawn. In its middle too, lessons are given, and at its end conclusions are drawn again, and the theme and the subject are interwoven and in harmony. The style of expression and the phrases are well-suited; from an artistic standpoint, the story is extremely captivating. But along with all these qualities, the events are based on reality and there is no exaggeration.

This story is fully related within a single surah, all together and complete. This is because the very nature of this story is such that it should be gathered together. For events unfold gradually: one day follows another, and one stage follows another. Therefore, conclusions could only be drawn from it if the story were presented in its complete form within one surah. If, like other stories, only some of its links had been brought, then the conclusions that emerge from the complete story could not have been drawn in that way. The manner of other stories in the Qur'an has been different; for example, the story of Bilqis, or the account of the creation of Maryam, the birth of Hadrat Isa (peace be upon him), or the event of the flood of Hadrat Nuh (peace be upon him), because some parts of these stories are themselves complete sections and links, and from them a separate lesson is derived. But the story of Yusuf is such that it must be read in its entirety in one sitting, and its narration from beginning to end in one place is also necessary.

﴿Nahnu naqussu 'alayka ... al-ghafilin﴾ (12:3) "We relate to you the best of narratives (qasas) by revealing to you this Qur'an, although before this you were certainly among the unaware."
